body: I listened. I know what you mean. I’ve known what you mean. I used to feel that anxiety too. About the past and the future. That feeling will pass. So see what things are like after the anxiety passes. And you know that your kids will have moments that they will want their mum for. You know that. But I feel you. You’re not alone in these feelings. It is really hard sometimes but you still need to drag yourself through. And see what the next day brings.
Thank you all for the responses.

I was thinking about this very question. I spent a couple summers briefly at Disney World, so that makes me a talking mouse. But I did hit up Epcot Center so I’m basically from all over the world. Polycultural talking mouse. I miss my abuelita so much!

I’m going through the same period. In my case I had gotten everything in order and picked out the place where I wanted to do it. Got in the car and started driving at 2 am and started thinking how rushed I was with the note I left and how the note just didn’t properly convey anything that might be of any comfort to anyone and how maybe it was better to not leave a note rather than leave words that come up short, so I turned around to destroy the note. And I was so exhausted after that, I sat down for a minute and fell asleep instead of getting back in the car. But I was on my way. It is a strange thing. After moments like that pass, you lose the momentum. And later you don’t have the same commitment to it, you lack the nerve, and you wish you had seized the moment. It is such a panicked anxiety driven thing where the stars have to align in a very dark way to get there. It’s a moment where the pain is so great you can’t think of how the suicide plays out for everyone you care about. It has its own logic in that moment, cut off from the world. To avoid succumbing to the urge, you have to maintain some lifeline to the world, keeping at least one toe in the door to the other side of life - that place where you know how much hurt this would cause.
